name: flow-statements-welcome-sender

deploy.description: Daily sender for the Flow Statements welcome sequence (Buttondown Basic has no Automations). Reads active rows due in the Welcome Sequence Zapier Table, re-checks each subscriber is still regular, and sends that step's private `imported` Buttondown email to that one subscriber. Then advances the row: offsets are days from confirmed_at (0, 4, 11, 18, 25), with catch-up sends at least 2 days apart. A row is paused, and the run goes red, after 3 consecutive send failures.

trigger.trigger_note: Daily at 9:00 AM account time (Asia/Singapore), weekends included; hourly until 2026-10-31. The tick payload is ignored; the clock comes from a ctx.step. Schedule by Zapier needs no connection.
trigger.cadence_note: Moved from hourly to daily on 2026-10-31. From 2026-12-01 every successful durable run costs at least 1 task, so hourly was ~720 tasks a month, nearly all of them runs with nothing due. Daily is ~30. Steps 2-5 are days apart, so they now go out at the first 9 AM run after they fall due. The welcome (step 1) is sent by flow-statements-welcome-enrol at confirmation, so it does not wait for this run; this Zap only retries a welcome that failed there.
trigger.params_note: `everyDay` takes `hod` (and optional `weekends`/`timezone_override`), not `moh`. If this ever goes back to everyHour, `moh` MUST be the string "00", not the integer 0.
trigger.manual_run_note: trigger-workflow <id> --input '{"dryRun":true}' lists what is due and what would happen. Add "only_email":"<address>" to handle one row, and "now":"<RFC3339>" to treat that instant as the current time (walk a test row through the sequence without waiting days).

connections_note: `buttondown_api` is the 'API by Zapier' connection holding the Buttondown API key, with its domain filter set to api.buttondown.com. sdk.fetch through it reads subscribers and makes the per-subscriber send; the official Buttondown app has no action for either.

tables.01M5M4KH7C1KCFD3CDRSAF46XA: Welcome Sequence — sequence state, one row per subscriber. Rows are created by flow-statements-welcome-enrol; this Zap reads status=active rows and updates them after each send. Columns: email (f1), subscriber_id (f2), confirmed_at (f3), next_step (f4), next_send_at (f5), last_sent_step (f6), last_sent_at (f7), status (f8), stop_reason (f9), fail_count (f10), last_error (f11).

enabled_note: Enabled by hand with enable-workflow on 2026-10-24 (sender first, then enrol), after both had shipped parked.
